transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Evan Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Maple Health), Carlos Vega (Maple Eng), Dana Lee (Maple Security), Markus (PM)

Auto-generated summary: Walkthrough of Redwood SDK quickstarts, auth options, and next steps to run simple benchmarks.

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intro — i'm ava from Redwood, and with me is evan on the se side who will run the walkthrough.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Hi, thanks — excited. quick thing, we're mainly evaluating for clinical-notes summarization and search embedding pipelines. throughput and P95 latency are our top concerns.
[00:30] Evan Chen: Great, today we'll do the python and typescript quickstarts, show auth patterns, env setup, and then a short demo against our hosted api. i'll call out optimize suggestions for cost too.
[00:45] Carlos Vega: Quick q — when you say hosted, do you mean the standard API or something like dedicated pools?
[01:00] Ava Martinez: Standard hosted api for quickstarts. we also discuss dedicated later — but for getting started, hosted is lower friction.
[01:15] Evan Chen: Alright jumping in — first slide is repo layout. quickstart lives at github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts. python example is under /python, typescript under /js.
[01:30] Evan Chen: For python the main file is quickstart.py. you pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, and then run. sample code is two calls: generate and embeddings.
[01:45] Priya Singh: For auth, does redwood support service principals or only api keys?
[02:00] Evan Chen: We have api keys for hosted, plus console sso for humans. for enterprise/private we support SAML/SSO and short-lived tokens. also we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in private deployments.
[02:20] Dana Lee: On KMS — do you support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for private? any HSM options?
[02:35] Evan Chen: Yes aws kms, gcp kms are supported for private installs. there's an HSM option via customer-managed HSM — we'll share the ops doc.
[02:50] Ava Martinez: i'll drop the security docs link after this call (SOC2, ISO, KMS guide).
[03:05] Evan Chen: Ok demo time. i'll run python quickstart: echo export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXXX; python quickstart.py.
[03:20] Evan Chen: (typing) you can see the generate call — we call client.generate(model="rwd-2-7b", input="Summarize clinical note...") and get streamed tokens in about 100ms first byte for small prompts on hosted.
[03:40] Priya Singh: 100ms first byte, what about p95 for 512-token responses?
[03:55] Evan Chen: p95 on hosted for that class usually between 400-800ms depending on load and region; we can share our perf profiles, and dedicated reduces variance.
[04:15] Carlos Vega: Are there sdk-level retry policies? how do we handle 429/503?
[04:30] Evan Chen: yes the sdk has exponential backoff by default and autos retry on transient 429s; we also expose hooks to customize. we recommend idempotency keys for generate streams if you need it.
[04:50] Evan Chen: switching to typescript quickstart — npm i @redwood-inference/sdk, set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, and run node quickstart.js. code sample shows streaming via async iterator.
[05:10] Markus: Any differences in feature parity between python and ts sdks?
[05:25] Evan Chen: parity is close — both support generate, chat, embeddings, rerank. typescript has better streaming helpers in node runtime, python supports async and sync.
[05:40] Priya Singh: for our infra we want secrets in vault. will the sdk pick up env vars from vaultsidecar or do we need to handle token refresh?
[05:55] Evan Chen: SDK reads env vars. for vault you run a sidecar that writes to env or file. for short-lived creds (enterprise) we have a token refresh endpoint and examples in the repo.
[06:15] Ava Martinez: quick note on best practices — set a per-route model pin and a fallback model to handle capacity spikes, and use prefix caching for repeated prompts.
[06:35] Evan Chen: also use batch embeddings for throughput — the sdk provides batch_embed helper that sends batched requests.
[06:50] Carlos Vega: can you show the console for where tokens/usage are displayed?
[07:05] Evan Chen: yep switching to console — (screen) the console shows per-route perf, token breakdown, and Optimize suggestions. there is a route page where you can pin model versions and set rollout policies.
[07:30] Dana Lee: where do we enable audit logs?
[07:45] Evan Chen: Audit logs are enabled in the private plane or dedicated; hosted offers limited audit trails but we can export logs to customer S3 for enterprise plans.
[08:05] Priya Singh: On billing — can you break out token costs for embeddings vs generation?
[08:20] Ava Martinez: yes on the billing page and in the usage api you get token-level cost breakdown. we'll send a sample estimate spreadsheet.
[08:40] Evan Chen: back to code — here's an example error handler snippet; we catch HTTP 429 and 503, then use sdk.retry() wrapper. here's a small code block.
[09:05] Evan Chen: (minor transcription noise) "and if you want streaming in typescript use for await (const chunk of stream) { process(chunk) }"
[09:25] Priya Singh: for embeddings storage we plan to use our own vector db (pgvector). any guidance on vector norms and dimensionality?
[09:40] Evan Chen: we'll share an optimize note — use our 1536-d embedding for semantic search, normalize on index time, consider approx nearest neighbor with 8-16 probe settings; we'll attach a short best-practice doc.
[10:05] Carlos Vega: if we do dedicated, what's the onboarding window and capacity commit?
[10:20] Ava Martinez: dedicated typically takes 4-6 weeks to provision depending on region and hardware. commits are monthly or annual — we'll send the dedicated one-pager.
[10:40] Evan Chen: small demo — i run a quick embed batch, showing latency numbers around 20-40ms per vector on hosted. (note: numbers vary)
[11:00] Dana Lee: about KMS key rotation — how is key rotation handled for private?
[11:15] Evan Chen: you control rotation in your KMS; we fetch wrapped keys and rotate transparently as long as new key versions are accessible. we'll share the ops doc.
[11:35] Priya Singh: are there guardrails for hallucinations or content filtering?
[11:50] Evan Chen: yes we have moderation hooks and safety policies; you can run evals via Optimize to set quality thresholds and get regression alerts.
[12:10] Ava Martinez: i'd like to show quickstart folder links — (posts link) https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts
[12:25] Evan Chen: moving on: env setup checklist: 1) install sdk, 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY or configure sso, 3) configure region via REDWOOD_REGION, 4) set MODEL_PIN optionally.
[12:45] Markus: what's MODEL_PIN used for?
[13:00] Evan Chen: pin the model and version at the route level so you don't shift weights during rollouts — good for repeatable perf.
[13:15] Carlos Vega: any recommendations for batching in our worker? we run a microservice that does real-time summarization at 50 qps.
[13:30] Evan Chen: use persistent gRPC connections for the runtime where possible and the sdk's batcher; tune max batch size and latency SLO. Optimize will recommend config for your workload after sample traces.
[13:50] Priya Singh: how do we run a benchmark with your team? do you accept workload traces?
[14:05] Ava Martinez: yes we can run a pilot — you'll share traces or a small dataset, we run a perf run on hosted/dedicated variants and return a report. that's usually a paid pilot.
[14:25] Evan Chen: quick note: make sure to scrub PHI in traces if sharing, unless under BAA and private site.
[14:40] Dana Lee: we need BAA for PHI handling — do you support that?
[14:55] Ava Martinez: yes we have BAA for enterprise/private deployments — i'll connect you with legal.
[15:10] Evan Chen: returning to code — here's sample typescript snippet for streaming with error handling. (paraphrase)
[15:35] Evan Chen: code shows a retry hook and sample backoff. also shows how to integrate with opentelemetry for traces.
[15:50] Carlos Vega: opentelemetry — do you export spans for token-level timing?
[16:05] Evan Chen: yes we have tracing hooks that report request-level spans and token emission events; sent to your tracing backend via collector.
[16:25] Priya Singh: what's the quickest way to get an estimate for monthly cost?
[16:40] Ava Martinez: send us a sample QPS and token profile, or run the local quickstart with a small batch and we'll extrapolate; we'll provide a cost sheet.
[16:55] Evan Chen: some gotchas — watch out for long context windows and unbounded system messages in chat, these increase token cost. use compressed prompts where possible.
[17:15] Markus: for auth flow demo — can you show console sso?
[17:30] Evan Chen: (screen) console settings -> single sign-on -> configure SAML. once enabled, you can map groups to roles and enable audit logging.
[17:50] Dana Lee: role-based access control details?
[18:05] Evan Chen: RBAC maps to console roles; for API access you issue service tokens scoped to routes. we'll send the RBAC matrix.
[18:25] Priya Singh: anything on data residency? we need EU-only for some datasets.
[18:40] Ava Martinez: private deployments can be region-limited; hosted has EU regions and you can request tenancy in specific region. we'll confirm region options.
[18:55] Evan Chen: quick tips for the quickstart repo — there are sample dockerfiles for containerizing the sdk calls, and a docker-compose for local testing.
[19:15] Carlos Vega: how do we handle secrets in k8s?
[19:30] Evan Chen: use k8s secrets or vault; the sdk supports file-based keys as well. for private we can integrate with your key provider.
[19:45] Priya Singh: what about model updates and rollbacks?
[20:00] Evan Chen: use route rollouts — canary percent then automatic fallback if quality drops. Optimize can monitor prompts and flag regressions.
[20:20] Ava Martinez: ok quick recap — we'll send: quickstart links, performance profiles, security/KMS docs, dedicated one-pager, and a sample cost estimate.
[20:35] Priya Singh: sounds good. we'll plan to run the bench next week and set the observability deep dive after we have numbers.
[20:50] Evan Chen: any other q's?
[21:05] Dana Lee: not for now — i'll collect SOC2 questions and send them to ava.
[21:20] Markus: can we get a short demo of Optimize suggestions?
[21:35] Evan Chen: briefly — Optimize looks at your traces and suggests batch sizes, quantization profiles, and caching strategies. we'll schedule a separate session.
[21:50] Ava Martinez: next steps as discussed — i'll follow up with links and schedule invites. thanks everyone.
[22:05] (call wraps, small crosstalk)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings e.g., "rwd-2-7b" as "rwd to seven bee" and small punctuation errors.
